title: Rapid determination of heterocyclic amines in ruminant meats using accelerated solvent extraction and ultra-high performance liquid chromatograph–mass spectrometry
author: Manful, Vidal, et al.
materials: Aliquots (50 μg/L) of working standard mixture of HCAs containing internal standard (TriMeIQx = 0.05 μg/mL) were used as quality control for the extraction of samples with the accelerated solvent extractor (Dionex ASE 350, Thermo Scientific, MO, USA). Briefly, 25 uL of 5000 μg/L (5 μg/mL) working standard mixture was mixed with 2.5 mL of 0.5 M NaOH in MeOH/Water (70:30 v/v) and incubated for 2 h at room temperature with stirring in a 5 mL beaker. Diatomaceous earth (1:2 v/w) was added to the mixture and the paste loaded into 10 mL stainless steel ASE extraction cells for extraction with pure methanol. The ASE extraction program was set as follows: 2 cycles, 5 min heating time, 80 °C extraction temperature, 160 s purge time, and 1606 psi static pressure. The extracted analytes in 20 mL of methanol were evaporated to dryness with a rotary evaporator and nitrogen gas at room temperature. HCAs were re-suspended in 2.5 mL methanol and filtered (Mini-UniPrepTM G2 syringeless filter, 0.2 μm, Whatman, Buckinghamshire, UK) prior to analysis by UHPLC-HRMS/MS. The ASE extractions were performed in quadruplicates (n = 4) for each working standard mixture.

The UHPLC-HRAMS/MS analysis was performed on a LTQ Orbitrap XL mass spectrometer with an automated Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system controlled by Chromeleon software (Thermo Scientific, MO, USA). A Luna C18 column (100 × 2.0 mm I.D., particle size: 3 μm, pore diameter: 100 Å) purchased from Phenomenex (CA, USA) was used for HCAs separation. The solvent system used on the analytical column was: H2O, 30 mM ammonium formate (pH 3.2) as solvent A and pure acetonitrile as solvent B. Chromatographic separation was carried out at 20 °C with a flow rate of 0.2 mL/min, and 10 μL of sample was injected in the instrument. The gradient used for separation was as follows: 0−1 min 10 % B, 1−3 min 10–20 % B, 3−6 min 20–30 % B, 6−9 min 30–40 % B, 9−12 min 40 % B, 12−13 min 40–50 % B, and re-equilibrated at 90 % A for 2 min. The Orbitrap mass spectrometer was operated in the positive ESI mode. The following optimized parameters were used for the Orbitrap mass spectrometer, sheath gas: 8, auxiliary gas: 2, ion spray voltage: 4.50 kV, capillary temperature: 320 0C; S-lens RF: 100 V; capillary voltage: 30 V, mass range: 100−1000 m/z; full scan mode at a resolution of 60,000 m/z; top-3 data dependent MS/MS at a resolution of 30,000 m/z and collision energy of 35 (arbitrary unit); injection time 15 min; isolation window: 1.5 m/z; automatic gain control target: 2 e5 with dynamic exclusion setting of 30.0 s. The mass spectrometer was externally calibrated to 1 ppm using ESI negative and positive calibration solutions (Thermo Scientific, MO, USA) prior to usage.

Working standard mixtures (20, 40 and 60 μg/L) of HCAs containing internal standard (TriMeIQx = 0.05 μg/mL) dissolved in 2.5 mL of 0.5 M NaOH in MeOH/Water (70:30 v/v) and incubated for 2 h at room temperature with stirring. Diatomaceous earth (1:2 v/w) was added to the mixture and the paste loaded into 10 mL stainless steel ASE extraction cells, and extracted with an accelerated solvent extractor (Dionex ASE 350, Thermo Scientific, MO, USA). Extracted analytes were recovered after roto-evaporation, resuspended in 2.5 mL pure methanol and analyzed by UHPLC-HRMS/MS on a LTQ Orbitrap XL mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, MO, USA) with an automated Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system as previously described for HCA standards.

HCAs were extracted with an accelerated solvent extractor (Dionex ASE 350, Thermo Scientific, MO, USA). Grilled meat (1 g) was ground, spiked with internal standard (TriMeIQx = 0.05 μg/mL), mixed with 0.5 M NaOH in MeOH/Water (70:30 v/v) and incubated for 2 h at room temperature. Diatomaceous earth (1:2 w/w) was added to the mixture and HCAs were extracted with pure methanol. The ASE extraction program was as follows: 2 cycles, 5 min heating time, 80 °C extraction temperature, 160 s purge time, and 1606 psi static pressure. The extracted analytes were evaporated to dryness with a rotary evaporator and nitrogen gas at room temperature. HCAs were re-suspended in 2.5 mL methanol and filtered (Mini-UniPrepTM G2 syringeless filter, 0.2 μm, Whatman, Buckinghamshire, UK) prior to ultrahigh performance liquid chromatography coupled to high resolution accurate mass tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS/MS) analysis [14].
The UHPLC-HRMS/MS analysis was performed on a LTQ Orbitrap XL mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, MO, USA) as previously described for HCA standards.

steps.title: Prepare HCA stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each HCA (IQ, MeIQx, MeIQ, TriMeIQx, PhIP, Harman, Nor‑Harman) to 1 mg mL⁻¹ in appropriate solvent, aliquot and store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Make calibration standards
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the stock solutions in acetonitrile:water (10:90 v/v) to obtain six calibration levels (5, 10, 20, 50, 80, 100 µg L⁻¹) in quadruplicate (n = 4). Add TriMeIQx as internal standard to a final concentration of 0.05 µg mL⁻¹ in each standard.

steps.title: Prepare QC working mixture
steps.instruction: Mix 25 µL of a 5000 µg L⁻¹ (5 µg mL⁻¹) HCA working mixture with 2.5 mL of 0.5 M NaOH in MeOH/Water (70:30 v/v). Stir at room temperature for 2 h.

steps.title: Add diatomaceous earth and load ASE cell
steps.instruction: Add diatomaceous earth to the above mixture at a ratio of 1 part sample to 2 parts (v/w). Transfer the resulting paste into a 10 mL stainless‑steel ASE extraction cell.

steps.title: Accelerated solvent extraction (ASE)
steps.instruction: Run the Dionex ASE 350 extractor with pure methanol using the program: 2 cycles, 5 min heating, 80 °C extraction temperature, 160 s purge time, 1606 psi static pressure. Collect the 20 mL methanol extract.

steps.title: Evaporate and re‑constitute extract
steps.instruction: Evaporate the methanol extract to dryness with a rotary evaporator, then dry under a gentle stream of nitrogen at room temperature. Re‑suspend the residue in 2.5 mL methanol.

steps.title: Filter re‑constituted sample
steps.instruction: Pass the 2.5 mL solution through a Mini‑UniPrep™ G2 syringeless filter (0.2 µm, Whatman, Buckinghamshire, UK).

steps.title: UHPLC‑HRAM/MS analysis – LC setup
steps.instruction: Install a Luna C18 column (100 × 2.0 mm I.D., 3 µm, 100 Å, Phenomenex). Use mobile phase A: water with 30 mM ammonium formate (pH 3.2) and mobile phase B: pure acetonitrile. Set column temperature to 20 °C, flow rate 0.2 mL min⁻¹, injection volume 10 µL. Apply the gradient: 0‑1 min 10 % B; 1‑3 min 10‑20 % B; 3‑6 min 20‑30 % B; 6‑9 min 30‑40 % B; 9‑12 min 40 % B; 12‑13 min 40‑50 % B; re‑equilibrate at 90 % A for 2 min.

steps.title: UHPLC‑HRAM/MS analysis – MS settings
steps.instruction: Operate the LTQ Orbitrap XL in positive ESI mode with sheath gas 8, auxiliary gas 2, ion spray voltage 4.50 kV, capillary temperature 320 °C, S‑lens RF 100 V, capillary voltage 30 V. Scan m/z 100‑1000 at 60 000 resolution (full scan) and perform top‑3 data‑dependent MS/MS at 30 000 resolution, collision energy 35, injection time 15 min, isolation window 1.5 m/z, AGC target 2 × 10⁵, dynamic exclusion 30 s. Calibrate externally to 1 ppm using ESI‑positive and negative calibration solutions.

steps.title: Prepare grilled meat samples
steps.instruction: Obtain 1 lb beef or moose strip‑loin steaks, cut into 1 g portions, and divide each portion into four replicates (n = 4). Grind each 1 g sample, spike with TriMeIQx (0.05 µg mL⁻¹), add 2.5 mL of 0.5 M NaOH in MeOH/Water (70:30 v/v), and stir at room temperature for 2 h.

steps.title: Extract HCAs from meat
steps.instruction: Add diatomaceous earth (1:2 w/w) to the meat slurry, load into a 10 mL ASE cell and extract using the same ASE program as for standards (2 cycles, 5 min heating, 80 °C, 160 s purge, 1606 psi, pure methanol).

steps.title: Post‑extraction processing of meat extracts
steps.instruction: Evaporate the methanol extract to dryness (rotary evaporator + N₂), re‑suspend in 2.5 mL methanol, filter through the 0.2 µm Mini‑UniPrep™ G2 filter, and submit to UHPLC‑HRAM/MS analysis using the LC and MS conditions described above.

steps.title: Method validation – accuracy & precision
steps.instruction: Prepare QC mixtures at 20, 40 and 60 µg L⁻¹ (same matrix as samples) with internal standard (TriMeIQx 0.05 µg mL⁻¹). Process them through the entire ASE‑UHPLC‑HRAM/MS workflow in quadruplicate. Calculate recoveries, intra‑day precision, LOD (3 SD/intercept ÷ slope) and LOQ (10 SD/intercept ÷ slope) as described.

steps.title: Assess matrix effects
steps.instruction: Spike post‑extraction meat extracts with standards, measure normalized peak areas (ratio to internal standard) and compute matrix effect (ME = B ÷ A × 100, where A = standard solution, B = spiked meat extract). Report suppression or enhancement for each HCA.
